question: Which party's member will GPS name as its candidate for Sarawak's Bawang Assan seat before nomination day on 28 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: GPS chairman Abang Johari said the full list of 82 GPS candidates will be announced on Nov 25, before the Nov 28 nomination cutoff, so 'none named' is small. Bawang Assan is a two-way fight. PDP holds incumbency (Wong Soon Koh), and its people won the seat against SUPP in 2021. PDP has submitted the seat and floats Joshua Ting, the Premier's political secretary. SUPP claims it as a legacy seat with Kevin Lau, and PBB Bawang Assan is on record backing SUPP (2024). Precedent: in 2021 GPS gave the former SUPP seat of Dudong to PDP's Tiong. Incumbency plus Ting's closeness to the Premier gives PDP a modest edge. No human prediction market was found (Polymarket/Manifold search: none).
sources: WebSearch results: theborneopost/utusansarawak/tvsarawak snippets on Joshua Ting and Kevin Lau (Nov 2026)
calls.dossier:
- Abang Johari (GPS chair), on 15 Nov 2026 (FMT/Malay Mail): GPS will announce all 82 candidates on 25 Nov 2026 at a PBB convention; appointment letters before 28 Nov nomination. In 2021 the list came out 2 days before nomination.
- On 15 Nov 2026 Abang Johari named 8 incumbents likely retained (4 PBB, 4 SUPP: Sim Kui Hian, Lo Khere Chiang, Wilfred Yap, Ding Kuong Hiing). Bawang Assan was not mentioned.
- PDP finalised 8 seats including Bawang Assan, Engkilili and Dudong (DayakDaily 15 Nov 2026; Borneo Post 16 Nov 2026). Deputy president Henry Harry Jinep says it is up to the PDP president and the Premier.
- SUPP submitted its list on 11 Nov 2026 and left Batu Lintang and Bawang Assan to the Premier; Sim Kui Hian: 'On Bawang Assan, the Premier will solve it' (DayakDaily).
- SUPP candidate: Kevin Lau Kor Jie, SUPP Central Youth chief and Bawang Assan branch chair, proposed by Sim in July 2026. In early Nov he deferred to the leadership.
- PDP option: Joshua Ting, PDP Youth chief and the Premier's political secretary for about 3 years, formerly a Sibu Rural District councillor. He said on 15 Nov 2026 (TVS/Utusan Sarawak) that he is ready to contest Bawang Assan. He breakfasted with Wong on 3 Nov 2026 amid succession talk. Incumbent Wong Soon Koh is a 7-term veteran.
- 2021 result: Wong (PSB) 5,952 vs SUPP's Robert Lau 5,039. PSB dissolved in April 2024 and Wong joined PDP.
- PBB Bawang Assan chief (May 2024) pledged to work with SUPP to win back the seat, which caused friction with PDP.
- DayakDaily, 17 Nov 2026: Bawang Assan, Engkilili and Dudong are traditionally SUPP seats; the article says SUPP 'has everything at stake'. In 2021 GPS fielded PDP's Tiong in Dudong.
- Status quo: the incumbent's party (PDP) holds the seat. No official GPS naming yet as of 17 Nov.
- Resolves off GPS's official naming (Abang Johari announcement or appointment letters), not off component-party statements.
- Event window: now -> 27 Nov 2026 16:00 UTC; the scheduled announcement date (25 Nov) falls inside the window.
- Searched but not found: any hint from the Premier on Bawang Assan specifically; any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold).
calls.reference_class: GPS (2021 Sarawak polls) allocation of overlapping/contested seats among components where the incumbent sits in a non-traditional component (e.g., Dudong to PDP); GPS general practice of renominating incumbents' parties

calls.reasoning: On 15 Nov Abang Johari said GPS will announce all 82 candidates on 25 Nov. Appointment letters come before nomination on 28 Nov, so 'nobody named before the cutoff' is very unlikely. The seat comes down to SUPP's claim that it is a traditional/legacy seat (Kevin Lau, endorsed by Dr Sim since July) against PDP's claim as the party of the sitting member (Wong Soon Koh is 84; the likely successor is PDP's Joshua Ting, who is the Premier's own political secretary). On 15 Nov PDP said it had finalised all 8 incumbent seats, Bawang Assan included. Reference class: when GPS has absorbed defectors who hold seats, the seat has usually gone to their new party (e.g. Dudong went to PDP in 2021). The Premier's personal tie to Ting also points toward PDP. On the other side, SUPP has pushed hard, Abang Johari has publicly backed Lau's bridge proposal, and 2021 was SUPP's own close loss. Small weight goes to a compromise candidate from a third party. No prediction market was found.

PDP formally submitted it among eight seats (Nov 15-16), and Joshua Ting, the Premier's political secretary, is the likely PDP successor. PDP has incumbency (Wong Soon Koh, ex-PSB, now PDP), formally submitted Bawang Assan on its 8-seat list, and its likely successor Joshua Ting is the Premier's political secretary. GPS precedent (Dudong given to PDP in 2021; ex-PSB incumbents keeping their seats) points the same way. calls.reconciliation: All four runs agree on the facts: GPS will announce on 25 Nov, PDP submitted the seat, SUPP left the seat to the Premier, Ting is the Premier's political secretary, and there is the Dudong precedent. The spread (PDP 0.55-0.59) is pure judgment about how much the incumbency precedent and Ting's tie to the Premier should outweigh SUPP's legacy claim and the trade possibility. Run 2 alone says Abang Johari publicly backed Lau's 'bridge proposal'; the other dossiers do not corroborate this and I cannot verify it, so it gets little weight. I take the incumbency-precedent reading as the one I would bet on, with a modest PDP edge. 'None named' is kept at 4% because the announcement could slip or the seat could be held back to the last moment, though the watikah ceremony falls before the cutoff.
